question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it begin as experimental/community support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: Adding FreeBSD is an operating-system support commitment across packaging, installers, services, docs, CI, release validation, and long-term ownership rather than a narrow source repair.

options.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
options.body: Approve only a staged plan that names the FreeBSD package/ports owner, installer/update path, service manager, docs, and smoke-proof expectations before advertising support.

options.title: Promote FreeBSD to Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD release ownership and split the work into tracked implementation tasks for packaging, service management, CI, docs, and validation.

options.title: Decline official FreeBSD support
options.body: Keep FreeBSD as community/source/npm use only and close the support-tier request after documenting that policy.

recommendation.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
recommendation.body: Approve only a staged plan that names the FreeBSD package/ports owner, installer/update path, service manager, docs, and smoke-proof expectations before advertising support.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses product tier, official support scope, installer publication, release validation, and ownership commitments.
